Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe a person who loves to grow plants

描述一个喜欢在家里或花园种植物的人

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a person who loves to grow plants (e.g. vegetables, flowers) at home or in the garden

  • Who this person is (这个人是谁)
  • What plants he/she grows (他/她种什么植物)
  • How he/she grows the plants (他/她怎么种)
  • And explain why he/she loves growing plants (并解释为什么他/她喜欢种植物)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a person who loves to grow plants (e.g. vegetables, flowers) at home or in the garden

I'd like to talk about my grandfather, who lives with us and is completely obsessed with growing plants. He's in his seventies and retired a few years ago, so he spends most of his time on the balcony, tending to his little vegetable garden. As for what he grows, it's mostly everyday vegetables: greens, scallions and a few chili pepper plants. He keeps them in foam boxes, which he lines up along the balcony railing, and they've actually grown into quite a lush little patch over the years. In terms of how he grows them, he's surprisingly methodical about it. Every morning, without fail, he waters each box and checks the leaves for pests, and he often talks to himself about which plants need more sun. He also saves seeds from one season to the next, which I find quite clever. The scallions we use for cooking at home are basically all from his boxes, and he's always proud to tell us how well the latest crop is doing. The reason he loves it so much, I think, is that it gives him a sense of purpose after retirement. He says home-grown vegetables are safer to eat, since he knows exactly what goes into them, and honestly, it's become his favourite pastime. Watching him, I can see that caring for those plants keeps him active and happy, and that's why I think it means so much to him.

讲的是我爷爷，退休后整天在阳台用泡沫箱种菜。种的是青菜、小葱和几棵辣椒，泡沫箱沿阳台栏杆排成一排。他每天早上雷打不动地浇水、检查叶子有没有虫，还会留种子。家里炒菜用的葱基本都是他种的，他总得意地跟我们说这茬长得多好。他爱种菜是因为退休后有了寄托，觉得自家种的菜吃着放心，也成了他最喜欢的消遣。

Q2What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?

I think there are several clear advantages. For one thing, it gives people access to fresh, chemical-free produce, which is healthier than what you often find in supermarkets. It's also a great way to relax, since caring for plants takes your mind off daily stress. On top of that, it saves money in the long run, and it makes the home look more lively and pleasant. So overall, it's a hobby that benefits both your health and your mood.

好处很多：能吃到新鲜无农药的菜，比超市的更健康；照顾植物还能放松减压；长期看省钱，家里也更有生气。总之对健康和心情都有益。

Q3Do many people grow vegetables or flowers at home in your country?

Yes, I'd say it's becoming quite common, especially among older people. In my country, many retired people grow vegetables on their balconies or rooftops, partly because they enjoy it and partly because they trust home-grown food more. Younger people tend to grow flowers or succulents instead, since they're easier to look after and look nice indoors. So while the trend is widespread, the style of growing differs a lot between generations.

越来越普遍，尤其老年人。很多退休老人在阳台或屋顶种菜，既因为喜欢也因为更信任自家种的菜。年轻人则更爱种花或多肉，好养又好看。趋势很广，但两代人的种法差别很大。

Q4Is it easy to grow plants at home?

It depends on the plant, to be honest. Some plants, like succulents and herbs, are very forgiving and basically grow themselves, so they're perfect for beginners. Others, like vegetables, need more attention, the right amount of sunlight and regular watering, which can be tricky in an apartment. That said, with a bit of research and patience, most people can manage it. I'd say the main challenge is consistency, since plants need care every day, not just when you remember.

看种什么。多肉、香草这类很好养，基本不用管，适合新手；蔬菜则需要光照和定期浇水，在公寓里有点麻烦。但只要有点研究和耐心，大多数人都能种好。最大的挑战是坚持，植物需要每天照顾。

Q5Why do people like to grow plants?

I think there are a few reasons. For many, it's a way to relax and slow down, since gardening is a calm, hands-on activity that takes your mind off screens and stress. For others, it's about the satisfaction of watching something you planted grow and thrive, which gives a real sense of achievement. And for some, especially older people, it's simply a routine that keeps them busy and gives their day structure. So the appeal is both emotional and practical.

原因有几个：很多人把它当放松方式，种花种菜是安静的手工活动，能让人远离屏幕和压力；也有人享受看着自己种的东西长大的成就感；对老人来说，它还是让日子有规律的日常。吸引力既有情感层面也有实用层面。

Q6Why do some people prefer to grow their own fruits and vegetables instead of buying them from the market?

I think the main reason is trust in food safety. Many people worry about pesticides and preservatives in store-bought produce, so growing their own gives them full control over what they eat. There's also the freshness factor, since you can pick vegetables right before cooking, which tastes noticeably better. On top of that, some people simply enjoy the process and the sense of self-sufficiency it brings. So it's a mix of health concerns and personal satisfaction.

主要是对食品安全的信任问题。很多人担心买来的菜有农药和防腐剂，自己种就能完全掌控吃进嘴里的东西；而且现摘现做更新鲜更好吃；还有人享受这个过程和自给自足的感觉。是健康顾虑加个人满足感的结合。

Q7Do you think choosing a college major is closely related to a future career?

To some extent, yes, but it's not a fixed link. For professional fields like medicine or law, the major directly determines the career path, since you need specific qualifications. However, for many other subjects, especially in the humanities, graduates often end up in completely different jobs, because employers care more about skills and experience than the exact major. So I'd say a major opens doors, but it doesn't lock you in, and lifelong learning matters just as much.

有一定关系，但不是固定联系。医学、法律这类专业领域，专业直接决定职业路径，因为需要特定资格；但很多其他专业，尤其文科，毕业生常常做完全不同的工作，因为雇主更看重技能和经验而不是具体专业。所以专业是开门，不是锁门，终身学习同样重要。
